#+title: CurupiraScript Design Document
#+author: Curupira Team
#+date: 2025-11-27
#+startup: overview

* Overview

CurupiraScript is an Elixir-to-JavaScript transpiler that converts Elixir code into modern JavaScript (ES2020+) for client-side execution in web browsers.

** Core Principles

1. Gradual Enhancement - Fork ElixirScript, modernize incrementally
2. Pragmatic Coverage - Support common Elixir features, not everything
3. Modern Output - Generate clean, readable ES2020+ JavaScript
4. Developer Experience - Fast compilation, good error messages, hot reload
5. Production Ready - Stable, tested, documented

** Goals & Non-Goals

*** Goals ✅

- Support Elixir 1.17+ (current stable)
- Core language features: modules, functions, pattern matching, guards, pipes
- Essential data types: atoms, lists, maps, tuples, structs
- Key stdlib modules: Enum, Map, List, String, Date/Time, JSON
- Modern Elixir syntax: stepped ranges, then/tap, Duration
- Fast compilation: < 5 seconds for medium projects
- Clean JS output: Readable, debuggable, tree-shakeable
- Good DX: Clear errors, source maps, hot reload support

*** Non-Goals ❌

- Full OTP support - No GenServer, Supervisor, processes (except basic Agent)
- 100% stdlib coverage - Only commonly used functions (~30% coverage is fine)
- Macro expansion - Use BEAM's pre-expanded AST
- receive/spawn - Client-side doesn't need process model (maybe in future)
- Backward compatibility - Breaking changes from ElixirScript are acceptable
- Multiple output formats - ES Modules only (no CommonJS, UMD)

* Architecture

** High-Level Pipeline

#+begin_example
┌─────────────────┐
│  Entry Modules  │  mix.exs: elixir_script: [input: MyApp]
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Find Used      │  Crawl module dependencies recursively
│  Modules        │  lib/curupira_script/passes/find_used_modules.ex
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Extract AST    │  Read from BEAM debug_info (macro-expanded)
│  from BEAM      │  lib/curupira_script/beam.ex
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Find Used      │  Tree-shake unused functions
│  Functions      │  lib/curupira_script/passes/find_used_functions.ex
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Translate      │  Elixir AST → ESTree (JavaScript AST)
│  to ESTree      │  lib/curupira_script/passes/translate/
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Generate       │  ESTree → JavaScript source code
│  JavaScript     │  lib/curupira_script/passes/output.ex
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Write ES       │  One .js file per Elixir module
│  Modules        │  js/Elixir.MyApp.js
└─────────────────┘
#+end_example

** Directory Structure

#+begin_example
lib/curupira_script/
├── curupira_script.ex           # Main API
├── compiler.ex                  # Compilation orchestration
├── state.ex                     # Compilation state (ETS-based)
├── beam.ex                      # BEAM file AST extraction
├── manifest.ex                  # Build manifest/cache
│
├── passes/                      # Compilation passes
│   ├── find_used_modules.ex
│   ├── find_used_functions.ex
│   ├── translate.ex             # Main translation entry
│   ├── output.ex                # JS code generation
│   │
│   └── translate/               # Translation modules
│       ├── form.ex              # General form translation
│       ├── module.ex            # Module translation
│       ├── function.ex          # Function translation
│       ├── clause.ex            # Clause translation
│       ├── identifier.ex        # Variable/function names
│       ├── helpers.ex           # Translation utilities
│       │
│       └── forms/               # Specific form handlers
│           ├── pattern.ex       # Pattern matching
│           ├── bitstring.ex     # Binary/bitstring
│           ├── map.ex           # Map literals
│           ├── for.ex           # Comprehensions
│           ├── with.ex          # with expressions
│           ├── try.ex           # try/rescue/catch
│           ├── receive.ex       # receive (maybe future)
│           ├── js.ex            # JS interop
│           └── ...
│
├── module_systems/              # Output formats
│   └── es.ex                    # ES Module formatter
│
└── lib/                         # Elixir-side runtime
    ├── agent.ex                 # Simple state management
    ├── js.ex                    # JS interop macros
    ├── functions.ex             # Helper functions
    └── string.ex                # String overrides
#+end_example

** JavaScript Runtime Structure

#+begin_example
priv/javascript/
├── lib/                         # Runtime library
│   ├── core.js                  # Core functions (Kernel.*)
│   ├── pattern.js               # Pattern matching engine
│   ├── types.js                 # Data types (Tuple, etc.)
│   ├── enum.js                  # Enum module
│   ├── map.js                   # Map module
│   ├── string.js                # String module
│   ├── list.js                  # List module
│   ├── date.js                  # Date/Time/DateTime
│   ├── duration.js              # Duration (NEW in 1.17)
│   ├── json.js                  # JSON module (NEW in 1.18)
│   └── ...
│
└── tests/                       # Runtime tests (JavaScript)
    ├── pattern.test.js
    ├── enum.test.js
    └── ...
#+end_example

* Implementation Phases

** Phase 0: Setup & Foundation (Week 1-2)

Goal: Get ElixirScript code running with modern Elixir/Erlang

Tasks:
- [ ] Fork ElixirScript codebase to =packages/curupira_script/=
- [ ] Update =mix.exs= dependencies:
  - [ ] Bump Elixir requirement to =~> 1.17=
  - [ ] Update =estree= to latest version
  - [ ] Remove deprecated dependencies
  - [ ] Add new deps: =jason=, =sourceror= (if needed)
- [ ] Fix compilation errors from dependency updates
- [ ] Get existing test suite passing
- [ ] Set up CI/CD for testing
- [ ] Update README with new goals

Success Criteria:
- ✅ All existing ElixirScript tests pass
- ✅ Compiles on Elixir 1.17 + OTP 26/27
- ✅ CI pipeline green

** Phase 1: Modern Elixir Syntax (Week 3-6)

Goal: Support Elixir 1.12-1.17 language features

*** 1.1: Stepped Ranges (1.12)

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
1..10//2  # => [1, 3, 5, 7, 9]

# JavaScript output
Elixir.Range.new(1, 10, 2).toArray()
#+end_src

Implementation:
- [ ] Update AST pattern matching for ={:.., _, [first, last, step]}=
- [ ] Implement =Range.new/3= in JS runtime
- [ ] Add tests

Files to modify:
- =lib/curupira_script/passes/translate/form.ex=
- =priv/javascript/lib/types.js= (Range implementation)

*** 1.2: Kernel.then/2 and tap/2 (1.12)

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
value
|> tap(&IO.inspect/1)
|> then(fn x -> x * 2 end)

# JavaScript
Elixir.Kernel.then(
  Elixir.Kernel.tap(value, (x) => console.log(x)),
  (x) => x * 2
)
#+end_src

Implementation:
- [ ] Add =Kernel.tap/2= to JS runtime
- [ ] Add =Kernel.then/2= to JS runtime
- [ ] Update pipe operator translation
- [ ] Add tests

Files to modify:
- =priv/javascript/lib/core.js=

*** 1.3: is_non_struct_map/1 guard (1.17)

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
def process(x) when is_non_struct_map(x), do: x

# JavaScript
function process(x) {
  if (Elixir.Kernel.is_non_struct_map(x)) {
    return x;
  }
  throw new Error("FunctionClauseError");
}
#+end_src

Implementation:
- [ ] Add guard translation for =is_non_struct_map=
- [ ] Implement in JS runtime
- [ ] Add tests

Files to modify:
- =lib/curupira_script/passes/translate/clause.ex=
- =priv/javascript/lib/core.js=

*** 1.4: Duration type (1.17)

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
duration = Duration.new!(hour: 1, minute: 30)
Date.shift(~D[2024-01-01], duration)

# JavaScript
const duration = Elixir.Duration.new({hour: 1, minute: 30});
Elixir.Date.shift(Elixir.Date.fromISO("2024-01-01"), duration);
#+end_src

Implementation:
- [ ] Create =Duration= struct implementation
- [ ] Implement =Duration.new!/1=
- [ ] Update =Date.shift/2=, =Time.shift/2=, =DateTime.shift/2=
- [ ] Add tests

Files to create:
- =priv/javascript/lib/duration.js=

Files to modify:
- =priv/javascript/lib/date.js=

** Phase 3: Developer Experience (Week 13-16)

Goal: Make development pleasant and productive

*** Better Error Messages

Current state:
#+begin_example
** (CompileError) translation failed
#+end_example

Target state:
#+begin_example
** (CompileError) lib/my_app.ex:42: CurupiraScript cannot translate this expression

    42 |   receive do
       |   ^^^^^^^ receive is not supported in CurupiraScript

Hint: CurupiraScript is designed for client-side code and doesn't support
      Erlang's process model. Consider using Agent for state management.
#+end_example

Implementation:
- [ ] Add error context to all translation failures
- [ ] Include source file and line numbers
- [ ] Add helpful hints for common issues
- [ ] Create error catalog documentation

*** Source Maps

Generate source maps for debugging:

#+begin_src javascript
//# sourceMappingURL=Elixir.MyApp.js.map
#+end_src

Implementation:
- [ ] Research ESTree → source map generation
- [ ] Add source map generation to output phase
- [ ] Test with browser DevTools
- [ ] Add =--source-maps= option

*** Incremental Compilation

Only recompile changed modules

Implementation:
- [ ] Enhance manifest to track file mtimes
- [ ] Skip unchanged modules
- [ ] Detect transitive changes (if A uses B, and B changes, recompile A)
- [ ] Add =--force= flag to bypass cache

*** Watch Mode Integration

Better integration with file watchers

Implementation:
- [ ] Emit compilation events
- [ ] Support external watch tools (exsync, mix_test_watch)
- [ ] Fast recompilation (< 1s for single module)

** Phase 4: Advanced Features (Week 17-20)

*** Protocols

#+begin_src elixir
defprotocol Renderable do
  def render(data)
end

defimpl Renderable, for: Map do
  def render(map), do: Jason.encode!(map)
end

# JavaScript
Elixir.Renderable.render(myMap)  # Dispatches to correct impl
#+end_src

Current state: ElixirScript supports protocols but implementation needs review

Implementation:

- [ ] Test with modern Elixir protocols
- [ ] Add support for =@fallback_to_any=
- [ ] Document limitations

*** Agent (State Management)

#+begin_src elixir

Agent.update(agent, fn state -> Map.put(state, :key, "value") end)
Agent.get(agent, fn state -> state.key end)
#+end_src

Current state: ElixirScript has basic Agent support

* Translation Strategy

** Data Types

*** Primitives

| Elixir | JavaScript | Notes |
|--------+------------+-------|
| =42= | =42= | Direct |
| =3.14= | =3.14= | Direct |
| ="hello"= | ="hello"= | Direct |
| =true= | =true= | Direct |
| =nil= | =null= | Direct |

*** Atoms

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
:ok
:error
:my_atom

# JavaScript
Symbol.for("ok")
Symbol.for("error")
Symbol.for("my_atom")
#+end_src

Utilities:
#+begin_src javascript
// Runtime helper
Elixir.atom = (name) => Symbol.for(name);
Elixir.atomToString = (sym) => Symbol.keyFor(sym);
#+end_src

*** Lists

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
[1, 2, 3]

# JavaScript
Object.freeze([1, 2, 3])
#+end_src

Note: Use =Object.freeze()= to prevent mutation

*** Maps

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir - atom keys
%{name: "Alice", age: 30}

# JavaScript
Object.freeze(new Map([
  [Symbol.for("name"), "Alice"],
  [Symbol.for("age"), 30]
]))
#+end_src

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir - string keys
%{"name" => "Alice"}

# JavaScript
Object.freeze(new Map([
  ["name", "Alice"]
]))
#+end_src

*** Tuples

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
{:ok, value}

# JavaScript
new Elixir.Tuple(Symbol.for("ok"), value)
#+end_src

Tuple class:
#+begin_src javascript
class Tuple {
  constructor(...elements) {
    this.elements = Object.freeze(elements);
    Object.freeze(this);
  }

  get(index) {
    return this.elements[index];
  }

  get length() {
    return this.elements.length;
  }
}
#+end_src

*** Structs

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
defstruct [:name, :age]

%User{name: "Alice", age: 30}

# JavaScript
class User {
  constructor(fields = {}) {
    this.__struct__ = Symbol.for("User");
    this.name = fields.name ?? null;
    this.age = fields.age ?? null;
    Object.freeze(this);
  }
}

new User({name: "Alice", age: 30})
#+end_src

** Control Flow

*** if/else

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
if condition do
  "yes"
else
  "no"
end

# JavaScript (simple)
(condition ? "yes" : "no")

# JavaScript (multi-line)
(() => {
  if (condition) {
    return "yes";
  } else {
    return "no";
  }
})()
#+end_src

*** case

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
case value do
  {:ok, x} -> x
  {:error, _} -> nil
end

# JavaScript
Elixir.case(value, [
  [new Tuple(Symbol.for("ok"), Elixir.var("x")),
   (bindings) => bindings.x],
  [new Tuple(Symbol.for("error"), Elixir.any()),
   (_) => null]
])
#+end_src

** Functions

*** Pipe Operator

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
value
|> transform()
|> process()
|> output()

# JavaScript
output(process(transform(value)))
#+end_src

Or with intermediate variables for debugging:
#+begin_src javascript
const _pipe1 = transform(value);
const _pipe2 = process(_pipe1);
const _pipe3 = output(_pipe2);
#+end_src

** Modules

#+begin_src elixir
# Elixir
defmodule MyApp.Users do
  def create(attrs) do
    # ...
  end

  def update(user, attrs) do
    # ...
  end
end

# JavaScript - js/Elixir.MyApp.Users.js
export default {
  create(attrs) {
    // ...
  },

  update(user, attrs) {
    // ...
  }
};
#+end_src

* Runtime Library

** Core (Kernel Functions)

Must implement commonly used Kernel functions:

*** Type Checks

#+begin_src javascript
Elixir.is_atom(x)
Elixir.is_binary(x)
Elixir.is_integer(x)
Elixir.is_float(x)
Elixir.is_number(x)
Elixir.is_list(x)
Elixir.is_map(x)
Elixir.is_tuple(x)
Elixir.is_function(x)
Elixir.is_nil(x)
Elixir.is_non_struct_map(x)  // NEW in 1.17
#+end_src

*** Operators

#+begin_src javascript
Elixir.add(a, b)          // +
Elixir.subtract(a, b)     // -
Elixir.multiply(a, b)     // *
Elixir.divide(a, b)       // /
Elixir.div(a, b)          // div
Elixir.rem(a, b)          // rem
Elixir.concat(a, b)       // <>
Elixir.append(a, b)       // ++
#+end_src

*** Other

#+begin_src javascript
Elixir.length(list)
Elixir.hd(list)
Elixir.tl(list)
Elixir.elem(tuple, index)
Elixir.put_elem(tuple, index, value)
Elixir.inspect(term)
Elixir.to_string(term)
Elixir.tap(value, fn)     // NEW in 1.12
Elixir.then(value, fn)    // NEW in 1.12
#+end_src

** Enum Module

High priority functions:

#+begin_src javascript
Elixir.Enum.map(enumerable, fn)
Elixir.Enum.filter(enumerable, fn)
Elixir.Enum.reduce(enumerable, acc, fn)
Elixir.Enum.each(enumerable, fn)
Elixir.Enum.find(enumerable, fn)
Elixir.Enum.all?(enumerable, fn)
Elixir.Enum.any?(enumerable, fn)
Elixir.Enum.count(enumerable)
Elixir.Enum.empty?(enumerable)
Elixir.Enum.member?(enumerable, value)
Elixir.Enum.at(enumerable, index)
Elixir.Enum.join(enumerable, separator)
Elixir.Enum.sort(enumerable)
Elixir.Enum.uniq(enumerable)
Elixir.Enum.take(enumerable, n)
Elixir.Enum.drop(enumerable, n)
Elixir.Enum.zip(enum1, enum2)
Elixir.Enum.with_index(enumerable)
#+end_src

* Testing Strategy

** Elixir Tests (Compiler)

Test the compilation pipeline:

#+begin_src elixir
# test/curupira_script/compiler_test.exs
defmodule CurupiraScript.CompilerTest do
  use ExUnit.Case

  test "compiles simple module" do
    result = CurupiraScript.compile(SimpleModule)
    assert result.status == :ok
    assert File.exists?(result.output_path)
  end

  test "handles compilation errors gracefully" do
    assert_raise CurupiraScript.CompileError, fn ->
      CurupiraScript.compile(InvalidModule)
    end
  end
end
#+end_src

** JavaScript Tests (Runtime)

Test the runtime library:

#+begin_src javascript
// priv/javascript/tests/enum.test.js
import { Enum } from '../lib/enum.js';

describe('Enum.map', () => {
  test('maps over a list', () => {
    const result = Enum.map([1, 2, 3], x => x * 2);
    expect(result).toEqual([2, 4, 6]);
  });
});
#+end_src

** Integration Tests

Test Elixir → JS round-trip:

#+begin_src elixir
# test/integration/basic_test.exs
defmodule Integration.BasicTest do
  use ExUnit.Case

  setup do
    # Compile test module
    CurupiraScript.compile(TestModule, output: "test/fixtures/js")

    # Run JS tests
    {output, 0} = System.cmd("node", ["test/fixtures/js/run_tests.js"])

    {:ok, output: output}
  end

  test "Elixir code produces expected JS output", %{output: output} do
    assert output =~ "All tests passed"
  end
end
#+end_src

* Glossary

- *AST* - Abstract Syntax Tree, tree representation of code structure
- *BEAM* - Erlang virtual machine that Elixir compiles to
- *ESTree* - JavaScript AST specification
- *Transpiler* - Source-to-source compiler (Elixir → JavaScript)
- *Tree-shaking* - Eliminating unused code from bundle
- *Trampolining* - Technique to implement tail-call optimization in JS
- *Mix* - Elixir's build tool
- *Hex* - Elixir package manager
